0.headline: Subscribe for Pranav Construction Ltd IPO; Anand Rathi
0.heading: Subscribe for Pranav Construction Ltd IPO; Anand Rathi
0.intro: Anand Rathi, has come out with its report on Pranav Construction Ltd The research firm has recommended to “ Subscribe” the ipo in its research report as on September 04, 2026.
0.body:
Anand Rathi, Pranav Construction Ltd
Incorporated in July 2003, Pranav Constructions Limited is a real estate company primarily engaged in redevelopment projects in the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) Region, with a predominant focus on the Western Suburbs. The Company was originally incorporated as Pranav Constructions Private Limited and was converted into a public limited company in July 2024. The company are the leading real estate company, based on the supply of units and number of completed and under construction MCGM - Redevelopment projects in the Western Suburbs, with a total of 1,864 units and 34 MCGM – Redevelopment projects (completed and under construction) whereas other developers have 4 to 11 MCGM Redevelopment projects, each launched between CY17 – Q CY26. The company are amongst the top redevelopment companies based out of Mumbai predominantly undertaking redevelopment projects in the Western Suburbs focusing on Economical, Mid and Mass, and Aspirational homes.

Valuation and Outlook
At the upper price band, the company is valued at 19.6x FY26 P/E and 12.7x FY26 EV/EBITDA, implying a post-issue market capitalization of ₹13,965 million. Given the company’s strong market position in the redevelopment segment, asset-light model, execution track record and healthy growth pipeline, we believe the valuation is reasonable considering the growth opportunities in Mumbai’s redevelopment market. Accordingly, we recommend a “Subscribe – Long Term” rating for the issue.

1.headline: Listed in 1995, delisted in 2010: Why Kanohar Electricals is returning to stock market with Rs 1000-crore IPO after 16 years
1.heading: Listed in 1995, delisted in 2010: Why Kanohar Electricals is returning to stock market with Rs 1000-crore IPO after 16 years
1.intro: Uttar Pradesh-based transformer manufacturer Kanohar Electricals is set to return to the stock market with a Rs 1,055.7-crore initial public offering (IPO) on September 8, 16 years after it voluntarily delisted its equity shares from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Delhi Stock Exchange and Uttar Pradesh Stock Exchange.
1.body:
Uttar Pradesh-based transformer manufacturer Kanohar Electricals is set to return to the stock market with a Rs 1,055.7-crore initial public offering (IPO) on September 8, 16 years after it voluntarily delisted its equity shares from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Delhi Stock Exchange and Uttar Pradesh Stock Exchange.

The company's shares were first listed on the three exchanges in 1995, but were subsequently delisted in 2010 citing low liquidity and trading volumes, according to its red herring prospectus (RHP).

The RHP filed by the company reads, "The equity shares of our Company were, in the past, listed on Bombay Stock Exchange (now known as BSE Limited), The Delhi Stock Exchange Association Limited (now known as DSE Estates Limited) and The Uttar Pradesh Stock Exchange Association Limited (now known as U.P. Stock and Capital Limited) on November 13, 1995, November 1, 1995 and October 31, 1995, respectively. However, thereafter, the equity shares of our Company were voluntarily delisted from Bombay Stock Exchange (now known as BSE Limited), The Delhi Stock Exchange Association Limited (now known as DSE Estates Limited) and The Uttar Pradesh Stock Exchange Association Limited (now known as U.P. Stock and Capital Limited) with effect from July 12, 2010, August 30, 2010 and October 20, 2010, respectively due to low liquidity and trading volumes."

The IPO documents identify low liquidity and trading volumes as the reasons for the company’s voluntary delisting from the three exchanges.

Kanohar Electricals will now seek to re-enter the listed market with a price band of Rs 601-632 per equity share. At the upper end of the price band, the issue values the company at around Rs 5,004.6 crore.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 300 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.19 crore shares by promoter entity K Sons Family Trust, amounting to Rs 755.7 crore at the upper price band.

Check IPO News Here

Investors can bid for a minimum of 23 shares and in multiples thereof. At the upper end of the price band, the minimum investment for retail investors will be Rs 14,536, while the maximum investment will be Rs 1,88,968.

The public issue will be open from September 8 to 10, with share allotment expected to be finalised by September 11. The company is likely to list on September 16.

As of March 2026, Kanohar Electricals had an order book of Rs 1,818.3 crore. The transformer business accounted for 83% of the company’s topline in FY26, while EPC contributed 16%. The remaining contribution came from other activities.

Kanohar Electricals reported a sharp increase in both revenue and profit in the financial year ended March 2026. Revenue rose 45.1% to Rs 653.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 450.6 crore in the previous year. Profit for the year nearly doubled to Rs 129.7 crore from Rs 65 crore in FY25.

The company operates in a segment that includes listed players such as Hitachi Energy India, Bharat Heavy Electricals, Schneider Electric Infrastructure, CG Power and Industrial Solutions, Transformers &amp; Rectifiers (India), and GE Vernova T&amp;D India.

Of the Rs 300 crore to be raised through the fresh issue, Rs 64.1 crore will be used for capital expenditure and other infrastructure-related requirements.

This includes purchasing new machinery and equipment, civil construction and interior development of an office building at the Gangol manufacturing facility, setting up solar power plants at its manufacturing facilities, and buying electric trucks and forklifts.

Another Rs 155 crore has been earmarked for incremental working capital requirements. The balance of the fresh issue proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

About Kanohar Electricals

Promoted by IIT alumnus Dinesh Singhal, Kanohar Electricals manufactures transformers and also undertakes engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) projects in the power transmission and distribution segment.

Its EPC operations allow the company to undertake turnkey projects involving substations and transmission lines, in addition to its core transformer manufacturing business.

The company operates two manufacturing facilities in Uttar Pradesh, located at Rithani and Gangol. Together, the plants have a transformer manufacturing capacity of 19,200 MVA.

2.headline: Deepa Jewellers IPO allotment today: GMP signals 10% listing gain; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.heading: Deepa Jewellers IPO allotment today: GMP signals 10% listing gain; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
2.intro: The allotment of shares in Deepa Jewellers’ Rs 459.72-crore initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised today, September 4, after the Telangana-based jewellery supplier witnessed healthy demand during its three-day bidding period.
2.body:
The allotment of shares in Deepa Jewellers’ Rs 459.72-crore initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised today, September 4, after the Telangana-based jewellery supplier witnessed healthy demand during its three-day bidding period.

The IPO was subscribed 42.61 times by the close of bidding on September 3, according to NSE data. Investors placed bids for 78.91 crore equity shares against 1.85 crore shares on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 105.96 times, while the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) quota was subscribed 37 times. The retail portion received 18.55 times subscription.

The IPO had a price band of Rs 168-177 per share and comprised a fresh issue of Rs 250 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of up to 1.18 crore shares worth Rs 209.72 crore. The shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on September 8.

Read Also: Rays of Belief IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar

The grey market premium (GMP) for Deepa Jewellers has fallen from the levels seen during the subscription period.

According to InvestorGain, the latest GMP stood at Rs 18 per share on September 4, implying an estimated listing price of Rs 195 at the upper end of the Rs 177 issue price. This translates into a potential listing gain of around 10.17 percent.

GMP is an unofficial indicator based on activity in the unregulated grey market. It can change before listing and does not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.

How to check Deepa Jewellers IPO allotment status

Investors can check their Deepa Jewellers IPO allotment status through Bigshare Services, the registrar to the issue, as well as the BSE and NSE websites. The basis of allotment is scheduled for September 4.

How to check Deepa Jewellers IPO via Bigshare Services

Step 1. Visit the Bigshare IPO allotment page at https://ipo.bigshareonline.com/ipo_status.html
Step 2. Select Deepa Jewellers Ltd from the issue list.
Step 3. Choose PAN, application number or beneficiary ID/DP-client ID as the search option.
Step 4. Enter the required details and submit to view the allotment status.

How to check Deepa Jewellers IPO via BSE

1. Visit the BSE IPO application page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
2. Select Equity under issue type.
3. Select Deepa Jewellers Ltd from the issue name dropdown.
4. Enter your PAN or IPO application number.
5. Click on Search to view the status.

How to check Deepa Jewellers IPO via NSE

Step 1. Visit the NSE IPO page at https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
Step 2. Select Equity &amp; SME IPO bid details.
Step 3. Choose DEEPA under the symbol list.
Step 4. Enter your PAN or application number.
Step 5. Submit the details to check the status.

Refunds and credit of shares to successful applicants are scheduled for September 7, while the stock is scheduled to begin trading on September 8.

Before the IPO opened, Deepa Jewellers raised Rs 137.91 crore from 14 anchor investors. The company allotted 77.91 lakh shares to the anchor investors at Rs 177 per share.

Motilal Oswal Finvest was the largest investor in the anchor book, acquiring around 20.3 lakh shares worth Rs 35.95 crore. WhiteOak Capital and 360 ONE each acquired around 5.08 lakh shares, with each investment worth nearly Rs 9 crore.

The anchor book also included Nomura Singapore, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust and Citigroup. Domestic mutual funds, including Tata Asset Management Company and Unifi Mutual Fund, were allotted around 14.96 lakh shares.

Deepa Jewellers will use the majority of the fresh issue proceeds to fund its working capital requirements.

Around Rs 215 crore has been earmarked for long-term working capital, including procurement, maintenance and scaling up of jewellery inventory. The remaining funds from the fresh issue will be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

The company is a business-to-business jewellery player that designs, processes and supplies 22-karat hallmarked gold jewellery to retail chains and standalone stores. It also undertakes job work and trades in silver ornaments, gold jewellery of other purities, precious stones and gold bullion.

The IPO had a lot size of 84 shares, meaning retail investors had to invest a minimum of Rs 14,868 at the upper price band of Rs 177. The issue opened on September 1 and closed on September 3.

Emkay Global Financial Services and Valmiki Leela Capital are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while Bigshare Services Private Limited is the registrar.

The company, incorporated in 2016, operates primarily as a B2B supplier across markets including Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Its product portfolio includes traditional and contemporary gold jewellery such as bangles, necklaces, earrings, rings and other customised ornaments.
